# On-call handoff — gateway 503 incident

**Prepared:** 2026-08-26 by <email>
**Source data:** `logs/gateway.log`, `logs/worker.log`, `deploys.csv`
**Status at end of log:** not resolved. The gateway was still failing.

---

## 1. Root cause

A gateway config change set `gateway.pool.perRequest` from `false` to `true`. Each request then took a private connection instead of a shared one. The connection pool holds 20 connections. It cannot serve that pattern. The pool exhausted itself and never recovered.

The log records the change 37 seconds before the first failure:

```
2026-03-14T02:13:41.234Z INFO  config    gateway.pool.perRequest: false -> true
```

Three facts support this cause:

- Every one of the 530 failures carries a paired pool error. There is no other error type in the file.
- Connection opens rose 100-fold. The log states `4180 opens in the last 5m, baseline is 40`.
- The pool queue only grew. `waiting` went from 0 to 172 and never fell.

**Confidence: high, but untested.** The correlation is exact. Nobody has tested a rollback. The same deploy also changed `gateway.timeout.upstreamMs` from 2000 to 2500. The pool errors point at `perRequest`, not at the timeout.

**Scope caveat.** This log is node-3 of 3. Check node-1 and node-2 before you assume the blast radius. The config change came from the deploy pipeline, so all three nodes are likely affected.

---

## 2. Impact window

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| First 503 | 2026-03-14T02:14:18.972Z |
| Last 503 in log | 2026-03-14T03:59:27.974Z |
| Confirmed duration | 1h 45m, and still open |
| Peak error rate | 83%, held flat from 02:20 |
| Total 503s in this log | 530 |
| On-call paged | 2026-03-14T03:21:05Z |
| Detection delay | about 67 minutes |

The log ends while the gateway is still failing. The end time above is the end of the data, not the end of the incident. Find the recovery time from a later log.

**Affected endpoints.** After 02:14, these five returned 503 on every request:

- `/v1/cart`
- `/v1/catalog/search`
- `/v1/checkout`
- `/v1/orders`
- `/v1/session`

`/health` continued to return 200 for the full window. This is why the error rate stopped at 83% and not 100%. **Health checks did not detect this outage.** Any alarm that watches `/health` stayed green through a total customer-facing failure.

---

## 3. Roll back this deploy

```
dep-4471   gateway   2026-03-14T02:12:00Z -> 02:14:00Z   a.novak
           config: connection-per-request for pool isolation
```

The deploy finished at 02:14:00Z. The first 503 came 19 seconds later. It is the only gateway deploy in `deploys.csv`.

### Procedure

1. Revert `gateway.pool.perRequest` to `false`.
2. Apply the revert to node-3 first.
3. Watch the `pool stats` line for 5 minutes. Confirm that `waiting` returns to 0.
4. Confirm that 503s stop on `/v1/checkout`.
5. If node-3 recovers, apply the revert to node-1 and node-2.
6. If node-3 does not recover, revert `gateway.timeout.upstreamMs` to 2000 as well.

Do not roll back `dep-4472` or `dep-4473`. Both shipped after the failure began. Neither can be the cause.

---

## 4. Open items for the next shift

1. **Two deploys went out into a live outage.** `dep-4472` shipped at 02:46Z and `dep-4473` at 03:25Z, both during an 83% error rate. Find out why the pipeline did not block them.
2. **`/health` does not test a real dependency.** It passed while every real endpoint failed. Change the health check to acquire a pool connection.
3. **A separate worker slowdown is open.** See section 5.

---

## 5. Not part of this incident

The workers did not hit the pool problem. All 1080 jobs in `logs/worker.log` succeeded. The worker pool held `size=8 in_use=1 idle=7 waiting=0` for the whole window.

The workers do have an unrelated problem. Job duration grew from 200ms to 2324ms across three hours, in a near-linear ramp. The ramp was already in progress at 01:00Z, over an hour before the gateway deploy. `db_wait` stayed flat at 5ms, so the database is not the cause.

Track this as a separate ticket. The log holds no cause for it. Worker logs from before 00:48Z will show whether `dep-4470` started the ramp.

---

Tell me if you want this saved to a file, or reformatted for your incident tracker.
